clue.text: A residence in which 28 's #1 was written

definitions.text: A residence in which 28 's #1 was written

parts.words: A residence in which 28 's #1 was written
parts.note: the clue reads as a home where a symphony was composed, but 'A' plus a residence also names the musical key of the composer's first symphony

explanation.surface: A biographical note about the house where the composer wrote his first symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's Symphony No 1 is in A flat, so the 'A residence' in which it was 'written' is the key, A FLAT, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a residence, and A flat is the key in which Elgar composed his first symphony.

clue.text: Twice supporting mum, fill it in

parts.note: supporting can be 'pro', the first of two words meaning in favour of
supporting can also be 'for', the second word meaning in favour of
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An instruction to back mother up twice while completing a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice supporting' gives two different words for the same idea, PRO and FOR, followed by MA for mum.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard printed form is a document whose blank spaces you are told to complete, hence 'fill it in'.

clue.text: Order to leave hat ornament for (28's?) ceremony

indicators.note: the order is told to depart from the hat ornament, so those letters are removed from it

parts.note: a pompom is a woolly ball decorating a hat
OM is the Order of Merit, an honour Elgar received

explanation.surface: A decoration is withdrawn from a hat for a grand state occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit (a British honour Elgar held), leaves POMPOM, the ball on a bobble hat; the '(28's?)' nods to Elgar's Pomp and Circumstance marches.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is splendid display and ceremonial show.

clue.text: Try to get drunk with it — half an oxide

indicators.note: being drunk means being muddled, so the letters of try and it are jumbled
half of the two-letter word an is its first letter

explanation.surface: An encouragement to drink, ending on a half-finished chemistry remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get drunk' scrambles TRY with IT (joined by 'with') into YTTRI, then 'half an' adds A.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttria is yttrium oxide, a white compound used in ceramics and phosphors.

clue.text: Astronomer's period can cruelly manifest

indicators.note: to manifest is to show in a new form, so the letters of can cruelly take another shape

explanation.surface: A remark that some astronomical cycle can show itself cruelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manifest' asks for the letters of CAN CRUELLY to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunation, the time from one new moon to the next, is a period astronomers measure.

clue.text: See 19
See 16
28's in game might be one of them

definitions.meaning: the composer's orchestral set of portraits of his friends

definitions.text: in game might be one of them
definitions.meaning: the two words are a rearrangement of a word for a puzzle

explanation.surface: The composer's piece might be one of several in some game.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the title as 'variations of ENIGMA': IN GAME is one such rearrangement of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enigma Variations is Elgar's orchestral work of fourteen portraits of friends.

clue.text: One launched into air aggressively as singer of 19/15/6 perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a surface-to-air missile fired at enemy aircraft
someone loyal to their country who would sing the anthem-like song

explanation.surface: Something fired skyward is compared with a person singing a stirring song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Patriot is an American air-defence missile; 19/15/6 is Land of Hope and Glory, sung at the Last Night of the Proms by flag-waving Britons.
explanation.definitionFit: A Patriot is a missile launched at aircraft, and a lover of their country might sing Elgar's song.

clue.text: Put the employees on a Scottish island

parts.note: staff are the people employed by an organisation

explanation.surface: An instruction to send the workforce out to a Scottish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFA is a small Hebridean island, home of Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: 28's five-month warning of August?

definitions.meaning: a ceremonial ... Elgar wrote for Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee
the month of the emperor Augustus comes five months after the third month, whose Ides were a warning to Caesar

explanation.surface: A composer's piece somehow linked to an advance notice given five months before summer.
explanation.walkthrough: August is named after the emperor Augustus, so it is the 'imperial' month; MARCH comes five months before it, and the Ides of March were the famous warning to Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's Imperial March of 1897 marked the Diamond Jubilee, and March precedes the emperor's month by five months.

clue.text: Again beat observable bottom

explanation.surface: A remark about spanking a visible backside a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games, to overtrump is to play a higher trump on a trick already trumped, beating it again.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge or whist, playing a higher trump than one already played defeats a card that had itself won.

clue.text: See 8
See 11
See 19
28's mad foreigners getting out for a change

indicators.note: something altered is changed, so the letters of mad foreigners and out are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crazy people from abroad leaving for some variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' links the fodder: MAD FOREIGNERS plus OUT, rearranged ('for a change'), gives all sixteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dream of Gerontius is Elgar's oratorio setting Cardinal Newman's poem.

clue.text: Russian horseman causing fire on Greek island

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the dismissal comes after the island

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: A Russian rider sets light to a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like setting alight, but here it means dismiss from a job; 'causing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were renowned cavalrymen of southern Russia and Ukraine.

clue.text: In a passionate way, I'm sly, cunning — and over the hill

indicators.note: the hill is laid across the jumbled letters, set into them
something cunning is crafty or devious, so the letters of I'm sly are worked into a new order

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone sly and cunning, and now past their prime, behaving passionately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunning' rearranges I'M SLY into SMILY, and TOR goes inside after the S; 'over the hill' looks like 'old' but gives the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormily describes acting with tempestuous, violent feeling.

clue.text: 28's rattled Adolf (and phrenology)

indicators.note: to rattle is to shake up, so the letters of Adolf, and, phrenology are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A dictator shaken up by the study of skull bumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattled' scrambles ADOLF AND PHRENOLOGY, all eighteen letters; the brackets are surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Land of Hope and Glory is the patriotic song set to Elgar's first Pomp and Circumstance march.

clue.text: Podgy women given a legal opinion

explanation.surface: Stout women receiving advice from a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: A fatwa is a ruling on a point of Islamic law, so 'legal opinion' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a formal ruling given by an Islamic scholar on a point of law.

clue.text: See 23
As 28 did in music lecture? His face did until Smith replaced him

definitions.meaning: a composer writes down musical pitches, as a student jots down points at a lecture

definitions.text: His face did until Smith replaced him
definitions.meaning: Elgar's portrait appeared on the twenty-pound banknote until Adam Smith's image took over in 2007

explanation.surface: A tribute to the composer, who scribbled at lectures and whose face once adorned banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's face was on the Bank of England £20 note from 1999 until Adam Smith replaced him in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer wrote musical pitches, a lecture student jots down points, and Elgar's portrait printed twenty-pound banknotes.

clue.text: Where to find 28's friends in a frame, or 8 13?

definitions.meaning: the dedication of the Enigma Variations is to 'my friends' portrayed in the music
a portrait in a frame is shown inside it

explanation.surface: A question about locating a composer's friends in a picture frame.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar dedicated the Enigma Variations ('or 8 13?') to 'my friends pictured within', each variation portraying one friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's friends are depicted inside the Variations, as a photo sits displayed inside its frame.

clue.text: Polish the second unknown stone

parts.note: in algebra x is the first unknown and y the second

explanation.surface: A Polish second-in-command unidentified, plus a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb, RUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red precious stone.

clue.text: He wrote this one of the 8 13

definitions.meaning: the setter of this crossword signs himself with this pseudonym
the ninth variation of Elgar's work, a portrait of his friend Jaeger

explanation.surface: The setter identifies himself with one of Elgar's musical portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: Nimrod, the mighty hunter of Genesis, stood for Jaeger (German for hunter) in Variation IX.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the pseudonym of this crossword's compiler and the title of Variation IX of the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: King of 28 and of Los Angeles Central?

indicators.note: Los Angeles is placed at the centre of the little word of

explanation.surface: A question about a king belonging both to the composer and to a Californian city's middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar wrote the cantata Scenes from the Saga of King Olaf; the second 'of' is opened up to take LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's cantata tells the saga of the Norwegian monarch named in its title.

clue.text: Such a Mastermind contestant might answer questions on Taj Mahal leather

parts.note: the Taj Mahal stands in Agra, in India
buff is a stout pale leather

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant might field questions about a famous monument.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a British TV quiz where contestants answer on a specialist subject; 'might answer questions on' links, and a buff is an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an enthusiast or expert, so someone specialising in India would answer on it on a quiz.
